Buildbox (YC S26) finds user-facing agent failures hidden behind successful traces and evals. The most expensive agent failures rarely look like errors. An agent can pass its evals and look healthy in traces while still failing to help users complete important tasks. They ask again, redirect the agent, try a workaround, or give up. Teams usually uncover these patterns after they’ve already affected customers. Buildbox is agent analytics built around user outcomes. We find where important journeys break down, show how often it happens and who it affects, and connect those failures to activation, conversion, and retention. Buildbox then tests better agent behaviors and product experiences, giving teams evidence-backed fixes to review and ship. Founders Mark Nour and Trishala Jain met at UC Berkeley and have been building together for the past three years. Across teams at Netflix, Google, Amazon, and MongoDB, they saw the same pattern: companies had plenty of signals & observability, but finding the issues that actually mattered and turning them into a fix still took a lot of manual detective work. Congrats on the launch, Mark and Trishala! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/g-BEkwhg

Arden (YC P26) is the AI-native platform for audit teams. At every public company, auditing still runs on spreadsheets and screenshots. Audit teams have to prove the company's controls are working, document how processes run, scope what to test, track issues, and report findings. They do all this work manually, and it's repeated every quarter. SOX compliance alone costs almost $2M a year at a public company, with most of that going to busywork. It's slow, expensive, and broken. Arden is rebuilding audit from the ground up with AI. Their platform works in your existing stack, with direct integrations and computer-use AI agents to capture screenshots from legacy systems that external auditors require. From there, Arden tests controls, documents processes, and produces audit-ready workpapers with full traceability. Auditors stay in the loop for review and judgement. If you work in audit, SOX, or accounting and want to spend less time on manual work, book a demo at ardentech.ai or reach out to founders@ardentech.ai Congrats on the launch, Aryaman Khanna and David Lomelin ! https://lnkd.in/gZ4smQZU

Arden (YC P26) is backed by Y Combinator. A few weeks ago, we got kicked out of three audit firms in one afternoon. David Lomelin and I were trying to talk to every internal auditor we could find. I scraped 800 contacts and set up a cold outbound sequence that accidentally sent them all at once. Berkeley banned my inbox by the end of the day. Email wasn’t an option anymore, so we figured we’d just show up in person. We grabbed boxes of Insomnia Cookies and walked into audit firms in SF’s Financial District. Most places turned us away. Two teenagers with cookies in audit firm lobbies, nobody knew whether to laugh or call security. We even tried pretending to be DoorDash drivers. But a few people actually sat down with us. What they described blew our minds, internal audit teams doing months of spreadsheet work that software should've killed years ago. The opportunity was way bigger than we realized. We applied to YC three weeks past the deadline. David and I didn’t think they'd even open it. Five days later, we were in the interview telling them what we'd seen. We might be the only 19 year olds losing sleep over SOX compliance. Every public company spends millions of dollars on it and nobody's fixed it. We’re building Arden, the AI-native platform for modern audit teams. If you're in internal audit or know someone who is, I'd love to connect.

Lance (YC W26) builds AI agents for hotel operations that manage guest communication, sales workflows, and on-property execution end-to-end. They’re already working with leading hotel groups in the US operating 50+ hotels across major brands. Hotels still run on phone calls for everything: towels, late checkout, maintenance, parking, and directions. Every request triggers a manual workflow, someone responds, gathers details, routes the task, tracks it down, and follows up. That model breaks when teams run lean. With 65% of hotels reporting staffing shortages, the front desk becomes the bottleneck. During peak periods or after hours, hotels miss up to 40% of inbound requests because the operation does not scale. Lance fixes this by handling guest communication 24/7, qualifying and responding to sales and booking inquiries, and coordinating real on-property execution. The system collects the right details, routes work automatically, escalates when needed, and supports multiple languages. Lance integrates with hotel systems and can take action through vision-based computer-use agents, so requests are resolved faster without handoffs. Every interaction is tracked and visible so staff stays in control, while Lance Pad connects housekeeping, maintenance, and service teams in real time, replaces walkie-talkies with structured communication, and ensures every request moves from intake → action → completion. Lance is being built with deep experience across AI, engineering, and hospitality. Caleb Chan built voice and AI agent systems at Google and Salesforce. Gatik Trivedi built voice models at Knowtex and worked on prediction models at Stanford. And Gavin Brennen brings engineering and product expertise coupled with growing up around Marriott hotel operations. If you’re a hotel owner, operator, or management group looking for faster guest service, fewer front desk interruptions, and more scalable operations, book a demo at lance.live or reach out to founders@lance.live . Congrats on the launch Caleb, Gatik, and Gavin! https://lnkd.in/dj5a2FJq

Built an AI compliance agent in 2 hours at the NVIDIA AI Agent Builder Hackathon — my first hackathon ever. Using LangChain, Llama 3.3.1, Brev.dev , and NVIDIA's API, my teammates Siddharth Veerapaneni , Ainur (Ann) N. , and I created a tool that lets users upload Laboratory Developed Test (LDT) documents and instantly checks them for FDA compliance — especially in light of the updated July 5th regulations. The agent supports multi-session workflows (think ChatGPT but task-specific) and offers real-time insights for regulatory teams. 🎥 Check out the demo here: https://lnkd.in/gK9N6qa7 As someone new to hackathons, this experience was inspiring. I got the chance to meet engineers and builders I’ve looked up to — including Carter Abdallah — and left with even more drive to keep building at the intersection of AI, healthcare, and compliance. What made it even more special? I met my teammates for the first time at the event. Despite having just two hours and no prior collaboration, we clicked instantly and built something we’re truly proud of. Huge thanks to NVIDIA and the Brev.dev (Acquired by NVIDIA) team for organizing, and shoutout to all the mentors who helped us bring this to life. Can't wait for the next one! #Hackathon #AI #LangChain #NVIDIA #LLMs #BrevDev #HealthcareTech #RegulatoryTech #FirstHackathon

Osseus (YC S26) is the intelligent development platform for robotics, bringing CI/CD across the mechanical, electrical, and software stack. The age of robots will not be unlocked by better AI models alone. Robot development still involves slow coordination across tools, teams, suppliers, requirements, and testing. Osseus makes this process agentic, compressing the iteration cycle and driving its avoidable cost to zero. Replace a drive motor and the bracket, wiring, electronics, firmware, requirements, and tests may all need to change. Each team sees its part, but nobody sees the complete impact until integration fails. Osseus connects into the tools a robotics team already uses (CAD, ECAD, GitHub, Jira, docs, test runs) and crafts a live dependency graph of the entire robot. It automatically maps each extracted requirement to the components, decisions, tests, and evidence that verify it. When something changes, Osseus traces the downstream impact, runs the relevant tests and simulations, prepares the hardware and software fixes on reviewable branches, and reruns validation before engineers approve and merge them. The Osseus Marketplace brings nearby component availability and lead times into the same design process. Builders can find compatible parts to buy or rent, compare their engineering tradeoffs, and keep prototypes moving. Teams and individuals can also monetize unused components by listing them. Founders Anish Mariathasan and Ayush Patel are Imperial College London engineering and computer science graduates. Between them, they have conducted robotics research at Imperial, ML research at a Harvard-HKU lab, and built agentic systems at Apple. If you build robots professionally or as a hobbyist, join the waitlist at https://osseus.ai , or email founders@osseus.ai ! Congrats on the launch, Anish and Ayush! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gp3_Mdin

I'm fly out to a cities to onboard customers in person. We could do this over Zoom. Most companies would. But sitting next to someone while they set up your product for the first time is a completely different experience. You see where they hesitate. You hear the questions they'd never type out in a Slack message. You catch the small things that turn into big problems later. Every time I've done this, I leave with 10x more context than I would have gotten on a call. At Autosana we have a rule: if a customer is getting started with us and we can be there in person, we will be. It doesn't scale. That's the point. The customers who feel taken care of from day one are the ones who stay, expand, and refer you to everyone they know. Compound interest but for trust 🫶
